title: Loro Parque Tickets: Types, How to Book and What's Included
metaTitle: Loro Parque Tickets: Types & How to Book (Guide)
metaDescription: Compare Loro Parque tickets in Tenerife: entry tickets, guided experiences and transfer options, and how to book your date in advance.
excerpt: The main ticket types, what each includes, and how to book your day at Loro Parque.
quickAnswer: Start with a standard entry ticket; choose a guided experience or transfer option if you want extras. Book online for your chosen date.

content.text: Loro Parque in Puerto de la Cruz is one of Tenerife's most popular attractions, and booking ahead makes the day simpler. This guide explains the main ticket types so you can pick the right one.
Standard entry tickets

A standard ticket gives general admission to the park, including its habitats, gardens and daily animal presentations. It suits independent visitors and families who want to explore at their own pace.
Guided experiences and premium options
Some options add a guide, meals or reserved seating at presentations. They cost more, so check what each one includes before choosing.
Transfer and combination options
If you are staying away from Puerto de la Cruz, a ticket with a return transfer saves driving. Some partners also sell combination tickets with other Tenerife attractions.
Before you book
Check the date, age tiers for children, what is included and the cancellation terms on the booking page.

title: Loro Parque Ticket Prices: What Affects the Cost
metaTitle: Loro Parque Ticket Prices: What to Expect
metaDescription: What affects Loro Parque ticket prices in Tenerife — ticket type, age, extras and transfers — and where to confirm current costs.
excerpt: Why prices differ between tickets, and how to compare value rather than just price.
quickAnswer: Prices depend on ticket type, age and extras such as guides, meals or transfers. Confirm the current price on the booking page.

content.text: Loro Parque ticket prices vary, and they can change by season, so treat any figure you read elsewhere as a guide and confirm the latest on the booking page.
What changes the price

The ticket type is the biggest factor: standard entry costs less than options that add a guide, meals or reserved seating. Age matters too — children usually pay less and very young children may enter free.
Comparing value
A higher price can be good value if it includes things you would otherwise pay for, such as a transfer or lunch. Use the comparison table on our homepage to see inclusions side by side.

title: Loro Parque Opening Hours and Best Time to Visit
metaTitle: Loro Parque Opening Hours & Best Time to Visit
metaDescription: Loro Parque opening hours in Tenerife, how to confirm current times, and the best time of day and year to visit.
excerpt: Typical opening hours, presentation times and when the park is quietest.
quickAnswer: The park is generally open daily, typically from around 9:30 AM to 5:30 PM. Arrive at opening for cooler, quieter habitats and confirm hours before you travel.

content.text: Loro Parque is generally open every day, with typical hours of around 9:30 AM to 5:30 PM. Hours and presentation schedules can change, so confirm them before you travel.
Best time of day
Arrive at opening to enjoy cooler temperatures and quieter habitats. Check the presentation timetable at the entrance and plan your route around the shows you want to see.
Best time of year
Tenerife's north coast is pleasant for much of the year. Weekdays are calmer than weekends, and school holidays are the busiest periods.
Plan your day
Allow at least 4–5 hours, bring sun protection and comfortable shoes, and book your ticket ahead.

title: How to Get to Loro Parque in Tenerife
metaTitle: How to Get to Loro Parque, Tenerife
metaDescription: How to get to Loro Parque in Puerto de la Cruz, Tenerife — by taxi, bus, car or organised transfer from the north and south of the island.
excerpt: By taxi, bus, car or transfer from Puerto de la Cruz and the rest of Tenerife.
quickAnswer: The park is on Avenida Loro Parque in Puerto de la Cruz. Use a taxi, bus or tourist train from town, or drive or book a transfer from elsewhere on Tenerife.

content.text: Loro Parque is on the edge of Puerto de la Cruz, on Tenerife's north coast, at Avenida Loro Parque.
From Puerto de la Cruz
The park is a short taxi, bus or tourist-train ride from the town centre. Walking along the coast is possible if you enjoy a longer stroll.
From the south of Tenerife
Allow an hour or more by car or bus, depending on traffic. A ticket with a return transfer avoids driving and parking.
By car
There is on-site parking. Check the current arrangements and any charges before you travel.

title: Loro Parque Attractions and Animal Experiences
metaDescription: What to see at Loro Parque in Tenerife: parrots, aquariums, penguins, animal presentations and gardens — plus tips for planning your day.
excerpt: The parrots, aquariums, penguins and presentations that make up a day at Loro Parque.
quickAnswer: Loro Parque is known for its parrot collection and also offers aquariums, a penguin habitat, animal presentations and gardens. Check presentation times on arrival.

content.text: Loro Parque began as a parrot park and has grown into one of Tenerife's most visited attractions.
Parrots
The park keeps one of the world's largest collections of parrots, in colourful aviaries and landscaped gardens.
Aquariums and marine habitats
Aquariums and marine habitats let you see sea life up close. Check which are open on the day of your visit.
Penguins
The penguin habitat recreates a cold-climate environment and is a favourite with children.
Presentations
Animal presentations run through the day. Collect the timetable at the entrance and build your route around the ones you want to see.

imageAlt: Aquarium underwater tunnel with stingrays and sharks

title: Visiting Loro Parque with Kids: A Family Guide
metaTitle: Loro Parque with Kids: Family Visit Guide
metaDescription: Tips for visiting Loro Parque with children: tickets and age tiers, what to bring, pacing the day and the best times to go.
excerpt: Age tiers, pacing, what to pack and how to keep little ones happy all day.
quickAnswer: Young children usually get reduced or free entry. Arrive early, plan breaks and pick two or three presentations rather than trying to see everything.

content.text: Loro Parque is a popular family day out, but it is a big park, so a little planning goes a long way.
Tickets for children
Child rates and free entry for very young children usually apply — the age tiers are listed on each booking page.
Pacing the day
Arrive at opening, take a lunch break in the middle of the day and choose two or three presentations rather than trying to see everything.
What to bring
Sun protection, water, comfortable shoes and a light layer for air-conditioned habitats.

content.text: Loro Parque sits on the edge of Puerto de la Cruz, one of Tenerife's longest-established resort towns.
Old town and seafront
Wander the historic centre and the seafront promenade, with cafés and views along the coast.
Gardens and nature
The surrounding area has botanical gardens and walking routes, easily combined with a park visit on another day.
Plan your trip
